events.credibility_reason: Claims finitude of Mersenne primes (a landmark) by 'elementary techniques' while the same abstract calls it open; self-contradictory abstract, unrefereed EasyChair venue, four versions within weeks, no expert uptake in ~2.5 years, and the claimed direction runs against the standard heuristic.

Landmark claim (infinitely many Mersenne primes) with no uptake in ~29 months; unrefereed, anonymous in the record, and the reported key step restates the open problem; the page itself could not be opened.

No argument and no exponents given; upload framed as a prize-priority timestamp; inconsistent publication status (under review vs published in Inventiones); claimed primes lie far beyond GIMPS's tested range and GIMPS lists no 53rd; no uptake.
A 'basic argument' for infinitude of Mersenne primes tacked onto a hypothesis-based note on an unrefereed EasyChair preprint, with no uptake in nearly three years.

Claimed nonexistence of odd perfect numbers (a landmark) with no uptake in nearly six years, repeated revisions, and the field continuing to publish odd-perfect constraints (e.g. Ochem-Zelinsky 2026) as if open.

events.ai_basis: AI systems (Anthropic's Claude, principally the Fable 5 and Opus model series, orchestrated in a multi-agent branch-synthesize-drill workflow with mandatory machine verification) carried out the computations, discovered and proved the lemmas, wrote and checked the Lean formalizations, ran the independent verification ledgers, and drafted the text.
ai_systems_credited: Anthropic's Claude, principally the Fable 5 and Opus model series

why: The statement asks only whether the set of perfect numbers is infinite. Infinitely many Mersenne primes would answer it in full (yes), so the Catalan-Mersenne, Chua and Zaman claims are scored whole; finitude of even perfect numbers (Vega) leaves the odd part open, and nonexistence of odd perfect numbers (Saeid-Nia) settles only the odd restriction, so both are case. All five are set aside as not_credible: each is a landmark claim on an unrefereed or self-archive venue, with no uptake over years, and each has its own red flags (self-contradictory abstract, no argument or exponents, prize-priority framing, a key step that restates the problem). The 52nd Mersenne prime is one more finite instance. Odd-perfect constraints (Ochem-Zelinsky, Mantovanelli) narrow where an odd perfect number could exist but bound nothing on infinitude, so they are none. Wagstaff and the SeqFan thread offer heuristics and conditional conjectures (none), and Ross and the quasiperfect paper address changed questions (variant). The quasiperfect paper's quote credits Claude with discovering and proving the lemmas, so its own row is generated, but it is a variant and carries no weight here.
doubts: Mantovanelli's reported ChatGPT 5.5 acknowledgement (typesetting, literature search, coding) was unconfirmed and would be none anyway. Several preprints.org claims (403) and other infinitude claims listed in 'incomplete' were never opened. Saeid-Nia could be read as none (a reduction) rather than case; it makes no difference because it is pre-snapshot and not credible.
